action_items: MEDIUM: Make AppSidebar responsive at mobile breakpoint (<640px) — force collapsed icon rail (~52px) so the dashboard main content has breathing room on 375px. Right now aside stays at 240px and clips the dashboard input + heading.
LOW: Empty-state heading 'No bracket created yet' is <h3>; consider promoting to <h1> for correct page heading hierarchy on /app (matches spec wording 'h1 + subtitle').
critical_code_review_comments: Sidebar component (/app/frontend/src/components/AppSidebar.jsx) likely uses a fixed 240px width with only an explicit collapse toggle; add a media-query/responsive `useEffect` to force collapsed=true under 640px viewport (or use a CSS `@media (max-width: 640px)` to override the width).

Spec said textarea class should be `.textarea-linear` but implementation uses `.textarea-brut`. Visual styling matches the spec exactly (idle hairline + violet focus ring + 3px violet glow), so this is naming drift only — either update the class name everywhere or update the spec wording. Low priority.

/faq is mounted inside MarketingLayout (no AppShell sidebar). When a logged-in user clicks the sidebar 'FAQ' link, the AppShell disappears and they land on the marketing FAQ. This is functional (ScrollToTop works) but UX-wise the user temporarily 'exits' the app — confirm this is intentional. If not, mount /faq inside AppShell as well, or render the FAQ component twice.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Marketing/app pages visually clean post brand-swap. Only outstanding issue is the mobile sidebar (240px on 375px viewport). After fix, re-run mobile_regression_375x812 block — expect aside width ≤ 60px and no clipping of dashboard input/heading. /faq route is intentionally under MarketingLayout (no AppShell) — sidebar disappears on FAQ navigation; this may or may not be desired UX.
rca of the issue: AppSidebar.jsx applies a fixed expanded width (likely w-60 = 240px) that does NOT respond to viewport width. The sidebar only toggles narrow/wide on the explicit user collapse-toggle action stored in localStorage. There is no automatic mobile-breakpoint override. Mitigation: in AppSidebar, add `useEffect(() => { const isMobile = window.matchMedia('(max-width: 640px)').matches; if (isMobile) setCollapsed(true); }, [])` OR add a CSS `@media (max-width: 640px) { aside[data-testid='sidebar'] { width: 52px; } }` so the rail is forced narrow on small screens regardless of localStorage value.
